public_rationale: Before the post, OpenAI and Google explicitly connected federal preemption proposals to state AI regulation. OpenAI pointed to hundreds of proposed state bills; Google sought to prevent fragmented state rules. This supports the ordinary causal reading that state regulatory momentum was a specific reason for their campaign. It does not establish an exclusive motive or a universal industry position.
limitations: The evidence establishes stated reasons, not independently verified private intentions.
Both submissions also invoke innovation and national competitiveness; they do not prove opposition to all accountability.

from_speaker: trying to shut the states down
our_interpretation: The claim concerns the preemption campaign underway when the post appeared on May 14, 2025.
The ordinary reading is that growing state AI regulation was a specific reason major technology companies sought federal restrictions on state rulemaking.
Support requires explicit links in contemporaneous submissions from multiple companies. It does not require proving that this was their sole motive.
The claim does not establish that every technology company supported preemption or opposed every form of oversight.
criteria.support_condition: Contemporaneous company submissions explicitly connect requests for federal preemption with existing or proliferating state AI rules.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Reliable contemporaneous records establish that the alleged preemption campaign or its asserted connection to state regulation was false.
